label: netPower Lite 8P

poe.note: MikroTik's specification table prints "PoE-out ports Ether1-Ether8", "PoE out 802.3af/at", "Low voltage PoE-Out current limit 1.0 A", "High voltage PoE-Out current limit 0.64 A" and "Total output power 120" - the 120 W ceiling is quoted, not derived, and the marketing copy repeats it as "120 W total PoE Output". Per-port ceiling is the current limit at the applied voltage, not a class, so no per-port wattage is declared.

notes:
Vendor figures from the MikroTik product page specification table (https://mikrotik.com/product/netpower_lite_ups - 200, 387,171 B, the netPower Lite 8P page: "Product code CSS610-8P-2S+OUT", read 2026-11-20), unless stated. 8x 10/100/1000 with PoE-out on Ether1-Ether8, 2x 10G SFP+, IP54 outdoor case, SwOS Lite, 88E6193.

WHAT WAS WRONG - the row declared `poe-pse`, `802.3af` and `802.3at` in `capabilities` but not one interface carried `poeOut`, and there was no `poe` block. The engine reads the PSE census from port hardware (scripts/audit-poe-budget.js), so this eight-port PoE switch had eight dry sockets and `show power inline` reported no budget at all. The eight copper ports now carry `poeOut`, and the published 120 W total is the `poe.budgetW`.

NOT MODELLED - the built-in UPS/battery charger and its 22-30 V battery input are power, not interfaces; no passive-PoE class is declared because the page prints only 802.3af/at.
